title: 10 Reasons To Smile, Breathe Easy, And Not Let Stress Get The Best Of You et-stress-get-the-best-of-you/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that most of the stress teachers feel comes from sources outside the classroom—new curriculum, policies, and constant change—and that the antidote is laid-back acceptance rather than resistance. He lays out ten specific payoffs of choosing calm over stress, ranging from effortless rapport-building to sharper student behavior and increased learning. The piece frames a teacher's emotional state as contagious, arguing that calmness settles students while agitation destabilizes them. It closes with a call to let outside pressures inform the teacher intellectually but never emotionally, protecting the energy needed for the classroom itself.
points: Stress from outside the classroom (policy changes, new programs) should be processed intellectually but never allowed to affect a teacher emotionally.
A calm, confident demeanor makes rapport-building effortless and causes excitable students to settle down.
A tension-free classroom is a better incubator for learning, boosting creativity, focus, and willingness to share.
A calmer teacher responds to misbehavior without anger, which strengthens leadership presence and classroom management.
Letting go of needless stress at school allows a teacher to be fully present for friends and family outside of it.
quotes: Much of the stress teachers feel today comes from sources outside of the classroom.
Here at Smart Classroom Management we believe that the best approach to anything beyond your immediate control is laid-back acceptance.
Excitability among students is a major cause of misbehavior, but not among teachers who carry themselves with an all-is-well vibe.
Stress inhibits concentration, participation, and performance. A classroom free of tension, on the other hand, is the perfect incubator for learning
Being in the classroom is challenging enough without allowing events and decisions beyond your control to affect your peace and ability to manage and inspire your students.
Accept what you can’t change. Learn what you need to learn. And save your passion, your enthusiasm, and your energy for the classroom.
